statement.text:
Champagne! (10 points)


Warning:
 Excessive alcohol consumption is harmful to health and drinking alcohol below legal age is prohibited.


Champagne is a French sparkling wine. Fermentation of sugars produces carbon dioxide (
\(\mathrm{CO_2}\)
) in the bottle. The molar concentration of 
\(\mathrm{CO_2}\)
 in the liquid phase 
\(c_\ell\)
 and the partial pressure 
\(P_{\mathrm{CO_2}}\)
 in the gas phase are related by 
\(c_\ell = k_\mathrm{H}P_{\mathrm{CO_2}}\)
, known as Henry’s law and where 
\(k_\mathrm{H}\)
 is called Henry’s constant.


Data




Surface tension of champagne 
\(\sigma = 47 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{J\cdot m^{-2}}\)


Density of the liquid 
\(\rho_\ell = 1.0 \times 10^3\,\mathrm{kg\cdot m^{-3}}\)


Henry’s constant at 
\(T_0 = 20\,^\circ\mathrm{C}\)
, 
\(k_\mathrm{H}(20\,^\circ\mathrm{C}) = 3.3 \times 10^{-4}\,\mathrm{mol\cdot m^{-3}\cdot Pa^{-1}}\)


Henry’s constant at 
\(T_0 = 6\,^\circ\mathrm{C}\)
, 
\(k_\mathrm{H}(6\,^\circ\mathrm{C}) = 5.4 \times 10^{-4}\,\mathrm{mol\cdot m^{-3}\cdot Pa^{-1}}\)


Atmospheric pressure 
\(P_0 = 1\,\mathrm{bar} = 1.0 \times 10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\)


Gases are ideal with an adiabatic coefficient 
\(\gamma = 1.3\)













Fig. 1
. A glass filled with champagne.

In the liquid, the concentration of dissolved

Since

solution.text:
Champagne: worked solution


This readable derivation follows the retained official solution, including its corrected factor of two in the diffusion growth law. Detailed examiner tables remain in the source PDF.


A.1


The Laplace pressure jump for a spherical gas-liquid interface is 
\(P_b-P_0=2\sigma/a\)
, so 
\(P_b=P_0+2\sigma/a\)
.


A.2


Growth requires the concentration in the surrounding liquid to exceed that next to the interface. At the critical radius, 
\(c_\ell=c_b=k_H(P_0+2\sigma/a_c)\)
. Since 
\(c_0=k_HP_0\)
, 
\[a_c=\frac{2\sigma}{P_0(c_\ell/c_0-1)}.\]
 For 
\(c_\ell=4c_0\)
, this gives 
\(a_c\simeq0.3\,\mu\mathrm m\)
.


A.3


For visible bubbles, neglect the Laplace correction to the pressure. The ideal gas law and the molar inflow balance give 
\[n_c=\frac{4\pi a^3P_0}{3RT_0},\qquad \frac{dn_c}{dt}=4\pi a^2j,\qquad \frac{da}{dt}=\frac{jRT_0}{P_0}.\]
 For model 1, 
\[a^2=a_0^2+\frac{2DRT_0}{P_0}(c_\ell-c_0)t.\]
 For model 2, 
\[a=a_0+\frac{KRT_0}{P_0}(c_\ell-c_0)t.\]
 The measured radius grows linearly, selecting model 2. A slope near 
\(0.24\,\mathrm{mm/s}\)
 gives 
\(K\simeq1.0\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m/s}\)
. The source accepts slopes from 
\(210\)
 to 
\(250\,\mu\mathrm{m/s}\)
 and 
\(K\)
 from 
\(0.9\)
 to 
\(1.1\)
 times 
\(10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m/s}\)
.


A.4


Upward buoyancy is 
\(4\pi a^3\rho_\ell g_0/3\)
 and downward Stokes drag is 
\(6\pi\eta av\)
. The gas weight is negligible compared with buoyancy. Terminal balance gives 
\[v(a)=\frac{2\rho_\ell g_0a^2}{9\eta}.\]
 Successive bubbles mark time steps 
\(1/f_b=0.05\,\mathrm s\)
. Measuring radii and displacements in the photograph gives a speed near 
\(4.5\,\mathrm{cm/s}\)
 for a radius near 
\(0.19\,\mathrm{mm}\)
, hence 
\(\eta\simeq2\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{Pa\,s}\)
. The official corrected acceptable viscosity interval is 
\([1.0,4.0]\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{Pa\,s}\)
.


A.5


Write 
\(q_a=da/dt\)
. Combining the terminal speed with constant growth gives 
\(dz/da=2\rho_\ell g_0a^2/(9\eta q_a)\)
. Neglecting the initial radius, 
\[H_\ell=\frac{2\rho_\ell g_0a_{H_\ell}^3}{27\eta q_a},\qquad a_{H_\ell}=\left(\frac{27\eta q_aH_\ell}{2\rho_\ell g_0}\right)^{1/3}\simeq0.39\,\mathrm{mm}.\]


A.6


The bubble count reaching the surface per unit time is 
\(N_bf_b\)
. Their total gas volume per unit time is 
\(4\pi a_{H_\ell}^3N_bf_b/3\)
. Using A.5, model 2, and the ideal gas law yields 
\[\frac{dc_\ell}{dt}=-\frac{18\pi N_bf_b\eta KH_\ell}{\rho_\ell g_0V_\ell}(c_\ell-c_0),\qquad \tau=\frac{\rho_\ell g_0V_\ell}{18\pi N_bf_b\eta KH_\ell}.\]
 Thus the excess concentration decays exponentially toward equilibrium.


B.1


For rim perimeter 
\(l\)
, the newly collected liquid volume is 
\(\delta V=hlv_fdt\)
. Its kinetic-energy gain is 
\(\rho_\ell\delta Vv_f^2/2\)
. Removing the film eliminates two liquid-air surfaces, reducing surface energy by 
\(2\sigma lv_fdt\)
. Only half becomes kinetic energy. Equating these gives 
\[v_f=\sqrt{\frac{2\sigma}{\rho_\ell h}}.\]


B.2


The cavity volume is 
\(V(t)=V_0+Sz\)
 and the adiabatic law gives 
\(P(t)=P_0[V_0/(V_0+Sz)]^\gamma\)
. Linearization gives 
\(P-P_0\simeq-\gamma P_0Sz/V_0\)
. Newton’s law becomes 
\[m_p\ddot z+\frac{\gamma P_0S^2}{V_0}z=0,\qquad f_0=\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{\gamma P_0S^2}{m_pV_0}}.\]


B.3


Use 
\(S=\pi r_c^2\)
, 
\(m_p=8\rho_gr_c^3/3\)
, 
\(V_0=4\pi a^3/3\)
, and 
\(r_c=(2/\sqrt3)a^2\sqrt{\rho_\ell g_0/\sigma}\)
 at the maximum frequency. Solving gives
